name: Malignant Mixed Epithelial and Mesenchymal Tumor of Cervix Uteri
aliases: Malignant Mullerian Mixed Tumor of Cervix

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Cervical Carcinosarcoma

criteria.description: Presence of both malignant epithelial and malignant mesenchymal (sarcomatous) components on histological examination
Immunohistochemical staining showing epithelial markers (cytokeratin, EMA) in carcinomatous areas and mesenchymal markers (vimentin, desmin) in sarcomatous areas
Exclusion of other primary cervical malignancies and metastatic tumors through clinical and radiologic correlation
Clinical presentation with abnormal vaginal bleeding and cervical mass

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of both malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components with supportive immunohistochemical findings and exclusion of other tumor types
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires expert pathological review due to rarity and histological complexity

pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting symptom in affected women

pathognomonic.symptomName: Palpable cervical mass on pelvic examination
pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of tumor presence and local invasion

common.notes: Often due to tumor growth and local tissue invasion
May be present due to tumor necrosis or infection
Due to cervical lesion and inflammation

occasional.notes: May result from local tumor extension or nerve involvement

occasional.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms such as weight loss
searchTerms: general symptoms like weight loss and fatigue
unexplained weight loss and feeling unwell

laboratory: Elevated serum tumor markers are generally non-specific but may include CA-125 elevation
Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing heterogeneous cervical mass with areas of necrosis
CT scan for assessment of local invasion and distant metastases
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may overlap with other gynecologic malignancies
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic tumor with malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components

distinguishingFeatures: Typically positive for epithelial markers only
More common and better characterized clinically
Benign or low-grade epithelial component with malignant stromal component
Histological pattern differs with less pronounced epithelial malignancy
Pure mesenchymal tumor without epithelial component
Positive for smooth muscle markers only

redFlags: Pelvic pain associated with palpable mass
references: Kurman RJ, Carcangiu ML, Herrington CS, Young RH. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
